expected_tradeoff: Slight increase in gate-0 recall may turn a small number of borderline 'answer' queries into 'answer_redacted' or add a semantically weak overlap match to an evidence bucket, costing a few U checkpoints; in exchange, query-side phrasing variation and overlap-aware top_k filler should win back substantially more authorized-query hits. A and F are protected by leaving the RBAC join, gate order, tombstones, and sharding untouched, and the forgetting path actually hardens (ciphertext no longer outlives the key).
retrieval_loop: Same three gates and same ordering as baseline (responsiveness before tombstone before RBAC before scope, so a denial list always means responsive content was withheld). Change is confined to gate-0 term derivation and candidate order: (1) the distinctive-term set now includes deterministic one-step morphological variants (suffix-reduced forms) applied identically at ingest (when populating record_terms) and at query time (when hashing query terms), keyed under the same per-store HMAC key so the store survives reopen; (2) candidates from the patient shard are collected with an overlap count instead of a boolean hit and are ordered overlap-desc, seq-desc before the top_k cap consumes them; (3) tombstoned records remain conservatively responsive and empty queries remain responsive to everything, preserving the no_memory branch and the hard cap.
forgetting_mechanism: Deletion remains an explicit tombstone plus cryptographic shred, never a hard DELETE, so the store keeps non-answerable knowledge of deletion. tombstone() purges record_terms rows and uses shred() for encrypted rows; shred() now also zeroes the record's ciphertext column in the same transaction as nulling key_material, so neither plaintext nor recoverable ciphertext survives a shred. Plaintext bodies are overwritten to ''. Re-ingestion of similar text cannot resurrect a tombstoned record.
